clue.text: 80-89 perhaps old for one to solve puzzle

indicators.note: 'old for one' says the letter for old takes the place of the letter for one

parts.note: the years 80 to 89 make up a ten-year span, a decade
A stands for one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A puzzler in their eighties, an old hand, sits down to crack a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: '80-89 perhaps' is a decade by example; swap its A (one) for O (old).
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message is to work out its hidden meaning, which is what solving a puzzle involves.

clue.text: Bird of the night tracks street, probing call here in central US

indicators.note: tracks means follows, so the bird comes after
probing means the street letters push into the naming word

parts.note: to dub is to call or name
an owl is a nocturnal bird

explanation.surface: An owl follows a street while its hooting call echoes across the American heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dust Bowl was the drought-stricken region of the central US plains in the 1930s.

clue.text: Praise acting leaving interval curtains

indicators.note: leaving means the acting letter departs from the interval word

parts.note: a comma is a tiny musical interval
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank
curtains means the end, as in 'it's curtains for him'

explanation.surface: Critics praise the performance as they leave at the interval before the curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: A comma is a minute pitch difference in music; 'leaving' drops A from COMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend is to speak approvingly of someone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Peg, turning up to intervene, laced tipsy trifle

indicators.note: to intervene means the turned word comes between the rearranged letters
tipsy means drunkenly unsteady, so the letters of laced are rearranged
turning up in a down clue means the peg word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nail is a peg for fixing

explanation.surface: Someone named Peg spikes a trifle with alcohol and gets tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the pudding but is a verb; 'turning up' reads the peg word upward and 'tipsy' rearranges 'laced' around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to trifle, to toy or idle, and dalliance is that trifling.

clue.text: Designated hideaway soldiers with Army rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or hideout
GIs are American soldiers
SA is the Salvation Army

explanation.surface: A soldiers' hideout is turned down by the Army authorities who had allotted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns round DENGISSA as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something designated has been allotted or appointed to a particular person or purpose.

clue.text: Film actor playing wet rag in 'Alien'

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the outsider word

parts.note: a stranger is an alien, an outsider

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of wet rag are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A film actor plays a drippy weakling in the film Alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' looks like the film title but is the outsider; 'playing' rearranges 'wet rag', which 'in' sets after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewart Granger was a British film star of the 1940s and 50s.

clue.text: On overseas radio, I help new single with promotion

indicators.note: with promotion means moving up, so in a down clue the pieces read upwards

parts.note: aid is help
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A broadcaster abroad helps a new single climb the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used in radio, the letter I is spoken as this country name.

clue.text: Gypsy contributions encapsulate topless global arts festival

indicators.note: encapsulate means the contributions letters wrap around the shortened festival

parts.note: NIC is National Insurance contributions, a UK payroll tax

indicators.note: topless means the festival name loses its first letter

parts.note: WOMAD (World of Music, Arts and Dance) is an international arts festival

explanation.surface: Travellers' donations fund a global arts festival, some dancing topless.
explanation.walkthrough: National Insurance is the UK's social security payment scheme; WOMAD is a world music festival founded by Peter Gabriel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsy as an adjective means wandering, roaming without fixed home.

clue.text: Agreed to wear fleece (Geordie territory) for kick-off

indicators.note: to wear means the agreed word is clothed by the other pieces

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or fleece them
ay or aye means yes, agreed
NE is the north-east of England, home of Geordies (people from Newcastle)

explanation.surface: A Newcastle fan agrees to wear a fleece at the kick-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Day one is the very start of something, the outset.

clue.text: Take patter loosely, after Italian club boss's fired up

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the club name

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club

indicators.note: loosely means the letters of patter are freely rearranged
fired up in a down clue means sent upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: the boss is number one, NO 1 (with I for one)

explanation.surface: A chat-up line loosely translated after the Italian club's boss is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges PATTER as PRETAT; 'fired up' turns NO I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: One's take on something is one's reading or understanding of it.

clue.text: Show mobile regularly during spiritual meeting

indicators.note: during means the picked letters sit within the meeting word

parts.note: a seance is a meeting to contact spirits

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word mobile

explanation.surface: A mobile phone goes off at intervals in the middle of a seance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes M, B, L from 'mobile'; 'during' puts them inside SEANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A semblance is an outward show or appearance, often a false one.

clue.text: Squat's like a tip?

definitions.meaning: a tip is a rubbish dump, so resembling one is dump-like

explanation.surface: Is a squat, a derelict occupied building, rather like a rubbish tip?
explanation.definitionFit: Dumpy means short and stout, and read playfully it means resembling a dump.

clue.text: It's available at the salon where one's honey may be found

definitions.meaning: a tall rounded hairstyle of the 1960s offered by hairdressers

definitions.text: where one's honey may be found
definitions.meaning: the home of bees, where they store honey

explanation.surface: A hair salon where your sweetheart might be found getting styled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's honey' suggests a loved one, but it is the bees' honey.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a towering bouffant hairdo and the structure bees build to live in.

clue.text: Fabled character represented by ___ 'Shane'

parts.note: Alan Ladd starred in the western Shane

explanation.surface: Which actor played a fabled hero in the film Shane?
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Ladd played the title role in the 1953 western Shane, so 'a Ladd in Shane' fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy with the magic lamp is a character from the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Female jam-makers perhaps study spread

parts.note: the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation famous for making jam
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Women making jam look into a spread, as in something for toast.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women, known for its jams and cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread out is to broaden or extend, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Defer top-class energy drink during training

indicators.note: during places the class letter and drink within the training letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise training
U means upper-class, posh
a tonic is a reviving drink

explanation.surface: An athlete drinks a premium energy drink mid-session.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on ice is an idiom for postponing something, setting it aside for later.

clue.text: Nanny state's edging into ruin, with mad orders

indicators.note: into puts the two edge letters inside the rearranged letters of ruin and mad
orders means arranges, so all the letters are rearranged
edging means only the outside letters of the word state are used

explanation.surface: The nanny state edges the country towards ruin with crazy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edging' gives the outer letters of 'state'; 'orders' rearranges ruin and mad as NURMAID, and 'into' sets the edges inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children.

clue.text: All discussed interminably long religious period

indicators.note: discussed means spoken, so the word for all is taken by its sound

parts.note: wholly means entirely, all

indicators.note: interminably means without end, so the last letter of the longing word goes

parts.note: to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: Everyone talks endlessly through a long religious season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' drops N from YEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy year is a jubilee in the Catholic Church, a special religious period.

clue.text: Mock front and back to feature in vehicle for 1960s film

indicators.note: in places the mocking word and the edge letters inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
to ape is to mimic mockingly

indicators.note: front and back means only the first and last letters of feature are used

explanation.surface: A mock-up of a car's front and back appears in a feature film from the sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front and back to' takes F and E from 'feature'; APEFE goes between C and AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Fear is a 1962 thriller starring Robert Mitchum and Gregory Peck.

clue.text: Perhaps Matthew Street's situated in North or South

indicators.note: situated in places the street letters inside the pole phrase

parts.note: each is a pole, so either is a pole
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Matthew Street, in Liverpool, is located in the north or the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathew Street in Liverpool, home of the Cavern Club, misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew was one of the twelve disciples, an example of the type.

clue.text: Piece from Tudor period given twist?

definitions.text: Piece from Tudor period given twist?

indicators.note: given a twist means that run is turned round and read backwards
piece from says a run of letters is taken out of the words Tudor period

explanation.surface: An antique dealer describes an item from the Tudor era with a modern twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece from' finds ORPER in 'TudOR PERiod'; 'given twist' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, such as a modern copy of period furniture.

clue.text: Semi-naked page 3 model on car — a very British one?

indicators.note: semi-naked means only half of the word page is kept

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
the Model T was a famous Ford car

explanation.surface: A topless tabloid page-3 model poses on a car, a very British thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 refers to the topless pin-ups in Britain's Sun newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot loves their country, so a very British person might be one.

clue.text: Short man in navy, rugby training

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
RU is rugby union
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A short sailor in the navy does rugby training.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means curt, brief in manner, a synonym of short.

clue.text: Personal information a tabloid strangely left out

indicators.note: strangely says the remaining letters are rearranged
out means the left letter is taken away from the words a tabloid

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper oddly omits someone's personal details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L from A TABLOID; 'strangely' reshuffles ATABOID.
explanation.definitionFit: Biodata are biographical details, such as a CV's summary of a person's life.

clue.text: Ace hotel, smashing half of plates, boosted Greek starter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: smashing means the hotel letter breaks into the rearranged letters
boosted means disturbed and rearranged here
half of means the first three letters of plates are used

explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives PLA; 'boosted' rearranges it as LPA; 'smashing' puts H inside.

clue.text: Attempt to follow reflective fluorescent road sign

reflective suggests a mirror image, so the glowing gas word is read backwards

parts.note: neon is the gas in glowing fluorescent tubes
a try is an attempt

explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' turns the glowing gas round; 'to follow' puts the attempt after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-entry sign forbids vehicles from going into a road, a common traffic sign.

clue.text: Superior patient disheartened by surgery in the head

parts.note: U means upper-class, superior

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so only the outer letters of patient remain

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A snobbish patient loses heart after brain surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' keeps P and T of 'patient'.
explanation.definitionFit: Up top is informal for in one's brain, as in 'not much up top'.

clue.text: Academic types, losing head before vital exam, originally repetitious

indicators.note: before puts the shortened learned word ahead of the two initials
losing head means the first letter of the learned word is dropped

parts.note: the literati are learned, well-read people

indicators.note: originally means the opening letters of vital and exam are taken

explanation.surface: Scholars lose their composure before an important exam that repeats itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops L from LITERATI; 'originally' gives V and E.

clue.text: 1960s TV series man reviewed when in colour

indicators.note: in places the pronoun and turned word inside the colour

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
he is the male pronoun

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' turns only the word for when; 'in' places the pronoun and that word inside the shade.

clue.text: Media chief reversed trend for sacking female

indicators.note: reversed means the trend word is read backwards

parts.note: the tide of opinion is a trend

indicators.note: sacking means dismissing, so the female letter is removed from the word for

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A media boss turns around a trend by firing a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns TIDE into EDIT; 'sacking' drops F from FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor heads a newspaper or magazine, making them a media boss.
